[[File:Richard Borg.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Richard Borg.]]
'''Richard Borg''' (born 1948) is a game designer.<ref name="wp-borg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Borg Richard Borg], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015192458/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Borg Internet Archive]</ref> [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]] planned Decipher's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game at his house in Florida.<ref name="bp-start">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=186s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 3:06–4:40. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> The [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] rules booklet thanks him "for rogue design in an elegant system."<ref name="2p-credits">[https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Introductory Two-Player Game Rules Booklet], Decipher / Parker Brothers, credits page. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015192404/https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Internet Archive]</ref>

== SWCCG planning ==

Braunlich and Tesh went to Borg's Florida house after the ''Star Trek'' CCG launch, before the Star Wars license was signed.<ref name="bp-start" /> Braunlich called Borg a friend and a game designer.<ref name="bp-start" /> They talked through how the game should play and whether it could hold the Star Wars universe.<ref name="bp-start" /> They returned with a general plan for the design.<ref name="bp-start" /> Braunlich's idea of using the draw deck as the player's Force came out of that planning.<ref name="bp-start" /><ref name="bp-force">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=280s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 4:40–5:12. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref>

== Later games ==

Borg was born in Connecticut in 1948.<ref name="wp-borg" /> He founded Action Designs in 1987.<ref name="dow">[https://www.daysofwonder.com/games/author/richard-borg/ Richard Borg], Days of Wonder. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015192424/https://www.daysofwonder.com/games/author/richard-borg/ Internet Archive]</ref> His games include ''Bluff'', ''Battle Cry'', ''Memoir '44'', and the Commands & Colors series.<ref name="wp-borg" /><ref name="dow" /> He entered the Charles S. Roberts Awards Hall of Fame in 2010.<ref name="wp-borg" /> In 2025 he designed ''Star Wars: Battle of Hoth''.<ref name="wp-borg" />
